messages:
elliot: Quick follow-up from last week's RFC about 'service strata'—we need a concrete migration runway to peel tenant concerns out of the router. Current router does: routing, billing enrichment, feature gating, and telemetry tagging. It's become a leaky abstraction.

priya: +1. Can we codify desired end-state in 3 bullets? My take: 1) single-purpose router surface (routing only), 2) independent enrichment lane(s) with explicit contracts, 3) rollbackable cutover path.

jason: Agree with the bullets. Also call out non-functional reqs: p95 latency must not increase >10% for top 5 tenants, no loss of billing tags, and observability parity within 0.5% sample difference.

aisha: Proposal: introduce three strata: decision-strata (routing/policy), enrichment-strata (billing/telemetry), and gate-strata (feature flags). Router becomes the decision-strata with small RPC to enrichment-strata for tags. Enrichment service owns writes to the event stream.

elliot: Important migration techniques: shadow-writes, dual-read validation, and staged canaries. We'll run shadow-writes from router -> enrichment for 2 weeks before switching flow. Shadow writes must be idempotent and cheap.

priya: Shadow-writes need dedupe keys. Suggest using request_id + tenant_id as prewrite id. Enrichment service responds with acceptance/duplicate.

jason: Concern: extra RPCs add tail latency. Can we use async prewrite to a local durable buffer (per-router ephemeral append log) and signal acknowledgement quickly to caller? Then background pump to enrichment-strata.

aisha: That prewrite pattern worked for other teams. Tradeoff: higher disk IO and complexity in router. Alternative: keep router thin and accept 8-12% p95 bump for initial canary while we validate. Which do we prioritize: infra simplicity or latency headroom?

elliot: Let's quantify. Run two microbenchmarks: A) thin-router + RPC enrich (baseline) B) router prewrite-append + background pump. Capture p50/p95, cpu, disk IO for both.

infra-bot: benchmark job queued -> https://ci.internal/benchmarks/1717200100

priya: Rollout plan suggestion: Week 0 (internal): shadow-writes on 0% traffic, validation only; Week 1: 1% production with fail-open enrich path; Week 2: 10% with fail-closed for canary tenants; Week 3: 50% ramp; Week 4: 100% and keep shadow-writes for 2 more weeks.

jason: Fail-open vs fail-closed explanation: fail-open means router will proceed without tags if enrichment fails (used early); fail-closed means we block and fallback to router's synchronous enrichment stub or fallback path.

aisha: For billing integrity we require at-least-once semantics for tags and idempotent downstream processors. We'll add prewrite ack + event dedupe id in the event envelope.

elliot: Testing matrix: unit tests for envelope id generation, integration replay with 7-day historical trace, canary chaos test (kill enrichment-strata for 60s), observability diff harness. Who takes ownership?

priya: infra-team owns decision-strata changes and benchmark harness; enrichment-team owns enrichment-strata impl and event contract. I'll make a cross-team playbook doc and link owners.

jason: Instrumentation: per-tenant meters: enrich_accept_rate, enrich_p95_ms, prewrite_queue_len, fallback_count. Dashboards and pager rules: page if enrich_accept_rate < 99% over 5m for prod tenants.

aisha: Security note: enrichment service needs read access to tenant metadata. Use control-plane minted short-lived tokens and minimal scopes.

elliot: Migration epic created -> REDWOOD-7890. I'll add tasks: harness, benchmarks, prewrite prototype, canary schedule, dashboards. arch-bot: epic created -> REDWOOD-7890

priya: Small config example for router RPC (so infra knows exact surface):
```json
{
  "router": {
    "enrichment": {
      "endpoint": "https://enrichment.internal/v1/enrich",
      "mode": "sync|async|shadow",
      "failure_mode": "failopen|failclosed"
    }
  }
}
```

jason: One extra operational guard: while shadow-writes are active, run a nightly reconciliation job that compares router shadow vs enrichment accepted events and emits mismatch reports. Threshold: <0.05% mismatch to proceed to next canary stage.

aisha: We should also plan a graceful rollback: keep enrichment-strata hot for 4 weeks after full cutover and keep routing toggles to instantly resume previous behavior. No DB migrations that are destructive until fallback window closes.

elliot: Action items and owners: infra (priya/jason) -> benchmark + router changes; enrichment (aisha) -> prewrite prototype + event contract; product-eng (elliot) -> playbook + canary schedule + reconciliation tooling. Target internal canary start week-of 2026-04-13.

arch-bot: playbook doc uploaded -> https://docs.internal/migrations/tenant-strata-playbook REDWOOD-7890

priya: I'll open PR for the thin-router config and bench results by EOD Thursday.

aisha: Enrichment prototype ETA end of next week, will ask for 1 extra backend headcount for 2 weeks.

jason: Sounds good. Thanks all. Quick sync after benchmarks land and we'll lock dates.

elliot: Thanks :rocket:
